name: Matengo
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Yoneda, Nobuko. 2000. A descriptive study of Matengo, a Bantu language of Tanzania. Tokyo University of Foreign Studies; also Yoneda, Tonal analysis of Matengo verbs; Tone Patterns of Matengo Nominals.

new_statements.quote: このように短母音と長母音は対立しているが，それとは別に，ポーズの位置の音節（以下「末尾音節」）が長母音以外の場合には，その前の音節（以下「次末音節」）の母音は常に長母音で現われる。[p. 27] … ただし，例5と6のように，末尾音節が長母音の場合には，その前にある次末音節の短母音は長母音化しない。[p. 28] … 本論文では「声調」という用語を用いているが，このような現象から考えると，この言語は「声調言語」というよりは，「アクセント言語」であり，アクセントがHで現われていると言えよう。[p. 51, fn. 16]
new_statements.translation: Thus short and long vowels are in opposition, but separately from that, when the syllable in pre-pausal position (hereafter 'final syllable') does not have a long vowel, the vowel of the syllable before it (hereafter 'penultimate syllable') always appears as a long vowel. [p. 27] ... However, as in examples 5 and 6, when the final syllable has a long vowel, the short vowel of the penultimate syllable before it does not lengthen. [p. 28] ... Although this thesis uses the term 'tone', judging from phenomena like this, this language is an 'accent language' rather than a 'tone language', and one may say that the accent is realized as H. [p. 51, fn. 16]
new_statements.citation: Yoneda, Nobuko. 2000. マテンゴ語の記述研究(バンツー系,タンザニア)：動詞構造を中心に [A descriptive study of Matengo, a Bantu language of Tanzania, with focus on the verbal structure]. PhD thesis, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.
new_statements.locator: Ch. 3 (音韻概要), §3.1.1 pp. 27-28 (penultimate lengthening) and §3.4.1 p. 51 fn. 16 (accent language); also §3.2.2 p. 43 (word-level shortening), §3.4.2 p. 53 (mora is TBU)
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.rule_in_words: Matengo is described as a tone language with a privative H (H marked and lexically/grammatically specified, L default), the mora being the tone-bearing unit; the author adds that it is better regarded as an accent language with the accent realized as H. The source never uses the word 'stress'. The stress-like prominence it describes is penultimate vowel lengthening: the vowel of the syllable before the pre-pausal syllable is always long, unless that final syllable itself contains a long vowel. The domain is the pause-delimited phrase (a noun followed by a modifier loses its own penultimate length and the phrase-final word's penult lengthens instead), not the word. Separately, at the word level, long vowels earlier than the antepenultimate syllable are shortened (p. 43).
new_statements.exceptions: No lengthening of the penult when the final syllable has a phonemic long vowel (examples 5-6, alé:/aló:). Phonemic long vowels are kept only in the last three syllables of the word; earlier ones shorten (p. 43). H on a 2-mora syllable normally falls on its first mora (F), variably on the second (R) (p. 53).
new_statements.domain_note: Pre-pausal (phrase-final) penultimate; examples show the lengthening shifting from the noun to the following modifier when the noun is not phrase-final (libá:gu vs libagu lilihú:la, p. 27). Hyman 2009 (second-hand, citing Yoneda 2005:394) likewise calls the unit of penultimate lengthening the tone phrase and the unit of shortening the word. Citation forms in the thesis are given as pronounced with a pause before and after (p. 55).
new_statements.identity_note: Yoneda's description is of Matengo (self-name Samatengo, Guthrie N13) as spoken in Litembo, Mbinga District, the historical centre of the Matengo area (main informant born 1932 in Litembo; the 1999 JAAS article used a speaker from Magu village); no dialect differentiation is made, so it maps to mate1258 itself. 'Samatengo' in Ndomba 2006 is the same language.

sources.note: No section on stress/accent as such. pp. 27-28: separately from the lexical short/long vowel contrast, the vowel of the syllable before the pre-pausal final syllable ('penultimate') always surfaces long, unless the final syllable itself has a long vowel (then no lengthening); Turuka 1983:6 is quoted as saying the penultimate vowel is phonetically long but not lexically contrastive. pp. 39-44: 2-mora syllables = phonemic long vowels, penultimate-lengthened vowels, vowels after CS and before NC; long vowels earlier than the antepenultimate syllable of the WORD are shortened. pp. 51-53: H vs L t…

sources.citation: Hyman, Larry M. 2009. Penultimate lengthening in Bantu: analysis and spread. UC Berkeley Phonology Lab Annual Report 2009, pp. 195-209 (quotes Yoneda 2005:394 on Matengo).
sources.note: Second-hand: Matengo has phrase-penultimate lengthening tied to phrasing/focus (citing Yoneda 2005), co-existing with a lexical length contrast and positional shortening; quotes Yoneda 2005:394: 'Long vowels... only appear in the antepenultimate, penultimate or final syllables of any word... the unit of the rule "vowel in the penultimate syllable becomes long vowel" is the tone phrase, the unit of shortening... is the word.'

sources.citation: Yoneda, Nobuko. [2017/2023]. Matengo (N13). In: Descriptive materials of morphosyntactic microvariation in Bantu (ILCAA, TUFS), 22 pp., CC BY 4.0.
sources.note: Morphosyntax questionnaire; only a one-line phoneme inventory (7 short + 7 long vowels) and a note that tone marking is given where available. Nothing on stress or length rules.

sources.citation: Yoneda, Nobuko. 2000. English resume of the same thesis ('A Descriptive Study of Matengo... with focus on verbal structure').
sources.note: Summarises ch. 3: H/L opposition, H marked, mora is the TBU; noun tone groups; default rule 'if there is no H in the isolated form of a word, the second mora of the word becomes H, but in two-syllable stems H appears on the word initial'. No mention of stress or penultimate lengthening.

sources.citation: Yoneda, Nobuko. 1999. マテンゴ語動詞の声調 (バンツー系, タンザニア) [Tonal analysis of Matengo verbs]. Journal of Asian and African Studies (Ajia Afurika gengo bunka kenkyū) 57: 133-155.
sources.note: Opening pages: Matengo has lost the tonal opposition in verb roots; tones are borne by moras, not syllables; phoneme inventory with long vowels; H/L/F/R notation. Nothing on stress in the pages read (article is on verb tone).

sources.citation: Yoneda, Nobuko. n.d. マテンゴ語における「母音挿入」 [Vowel insertion in Matengo]. 大阪女学院短期大学紀要 (Osaka Jogakuin Junior College Kiyō) 32, 17 pp.
sources.note: Morphophonological paper on epenthetic vowels at morpheme boundaries; states only that the language is a tone language and omits tone marking. Nothing on stress.
